what: A @defer block tells Angular to put the components inside it into a separate chunk and load it later, on a trigger such as idle time, entering the viewport or a click. With server rendering, incremental hydration uses the same blocks to wake parts of the page up only when needed.
like: Like packing only today's books in your school bag and fetching the others from the locker the moment the timetable says you need them.
why: Smaller first download, so the first screen appears sooner
Heavy widgets (charts, editors) cost nothing until used
Server-rendered pages can become interactive piece by piece

steps.d: Put a component, directive or pipe inside @defer. Angular splits their code into its own chunk, provided they are standalone.
@placeholder renders before the trigger fires. Its minimum parameter keeps it on screen long enough to avoid flicker.
on idle is the default. Others: viewport, interaction, hover, immediate, timer, and when <condition>. Several triggers separated by semicolons act as OR.
prefetch on idle downloads the chunk early while the content still renders on interaction, so the click feels instant.
@loading (with after and minimum timers) covers the wait; @error covers a failed fetch.
With SSR, hydrate on triggers keep server HTML static until a trigger fires; events before that are queued and replayed.

numbers.l: on-triggers (idle, viewport, interaction, hover, immediate, timer) plus the when condition
hydrate on triggers for incremental hydration, in 3 trigger types (on, when, never)
docs example for @loading after and minimum, to avoid flashing a spinner

choices.d: viewport for below-the-fold sections, interaction or hover for things a user must ask for, idle for nice-to-haves. Avoid immediate, timer and viewport on content visible at load: it can raise layout shift.
Combine a cheap render trigger with prefetch on idle so the code is already there when the user acts.
Routes split by page; @defer splits inside a page. Use both: lazy routes for screens, @defer for heavy widgets.
Plain SSR renders the placeholder only. Incremental hydration renders main content on the server and hydrates blocks on demand.

instead.why: The general idea of dynamic import and chunks that @defer builds on
Other ways to hydrate a page in parts

breaks.d: Deferring content visible on first load, or a placeholder with a different size.
breaks.see: CLS worsens in lab and field data
breaks.fix: Do not defer above-the-fold content; give the placeholder the same dimensions

breaks.d: A deferred component is also referenced outside the block, in a ViewChild query, or imported via a barrel file.
breaks.see: Bundle analyser shows no size drop
breaks.fix: Reference it only inside @defer and import from the component file directly

breaks.d: Nested @defer blocks with the same trigger fire together or in a waterfall.
breaks.fix: Give nested blocks different triggers and prefetch

say: I defer heavy, below-the-fold or on-demand widgets with @defer on viewport or interaction, and prefetch on idle so it still feels instant.
I keep above-the-fold content out of @defer and size the placeholder to match, to protect layout shift.
With SSR I use incremental hydration so the server renders the page and each block hydrates on its own trigger, with events replayed.

followups.q: What happens to @defer on the server?
followups.a: The placeholder is rendered and triggers do not run. With incremental hydration, main content renders on the server and hydrate triggers wake blocks later.

followups.q: How do you prove it helped?
followups.a: Compare the initial bundle size and LCP, INP and CLS before and after, using a bundle analyser and field data.

today: Incremental hydration is on by default whenever provideClientHydration() is used, with event replay included, so deferred blocks double as hydration boundaries in current Angular.

check.q: Which trigger is the default for @defer?
check.why: If no trigger is given Angular uses on idle.

check.q: What must a deferred component be to leave the main bundle?
check.a: Standalone and referenced only inside the block
check.why: Non-standalone or externally referenced dependencies load eagerly.

check.a: It can increase cumulative layout shift
